affinity_notes: On a CPU with performance and efficiency cores, Windows may run a kernel step started from FreeCAD or a hook on the slow cores at about a third of the speed. kit.sh() pins every subprocess it starts to `affinity_mask` (hex, e.g. "0xFFFF" = logical CPUs 0-15 when those are the performance cores) and raises it to `priority`. Blank (the default) = no pinning. A mask naming more CPUs than the machine has is skipped.
notes: freecadcmd_candidates: the first path that exists is used (a candidate may be a glob); put your own FreeCAD's FreeCADCmd first if it is installed elsewhere, or set KIT_FREECAD to the binary. python: blank = the interpreter that runs kit.py (the one the installer wired into the hooks); set it only to name a different one in the PowerShell lines `kit ps` generates. scratch: the folder whose disk is checked for min_free_gb before a run. timeout_s: the cap on one kernel step (KIT_TIMEOUT in the environment overrides it); timeout_check_s: `kit check` alone (it tessellates two bodies, three maps and a footprint sweep) - give the Bash tool its longest timeout (600000 ms) for it, or run it in the background.
